title: Touch lightly with two index fingers. Aristotle’s experiment. One or two? Necessity is that in virtue of which it is impossible that one can be otherwise. Argal, one hat is one hat.
html_source:
Internal narrative.

Firstly from Aristotle Problemata –
Why is it that an object which is held between two
crossed fingers 5 appears to be two ? Is it because we
touch it at two sentient points ? For when we hold the
hand in its natural position we cannot touch an object
with the outer 7 sides of the two fingers.

Secondly –

Necessity is that in virtue of which it is impossible that one can be otherwise. Argal, one hat is one hat.

is a fusion of two quotes from Aristotle Metaphysics, Book Gamma*, (Gifford).

Argal – therefore , a reference to :

http://lit.genius.com/2465463
